title: Epic Dunks On Steam With Vibe-Coded Storefront And Gets Roasted: 'This Launcher Is So F*cking Vibeslopped Its Funny'
key_facts: Epic Games released a preview of a rebuilt Epic Games Launcher and said in its announcement that it was 'vibe coded' with AI.
Epic's X account claimed the new launcher is faster than Valve's Steam, with a graphic of responsiveness benchmarks.
Epic Games Store general manager Martin Keely told IGN it is a complete rewrite of the shell and the store pages.
Users online mocked the framing and reported bugs, for example Fortnite opening UEFN after a graphics-mode change.
Kotaku says Epic told its own developers a week earlier to go 'AI first'.
Epic also announced Fortnite is coming to Linux through Proton, a compatibility layer made by Valve.
Epic CEO Tim Sweeney said Epic is retooling 'for maximum AI acceleration'; the preview carries a warning that beta issues are possible.
quote_evidence: "Programming is hard," the company wrote in its official announcement post... "So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that's way faster and more responsive than the current one."
"It's been rebuilt entirely from the ground up," Epic Games Store general manager Martin Keely told IGN.
"The new Epic Games Launcher is in Preview for testing, and with any beta there could be issues," reads the disclaimer.
why_it_matters_hint: A big game company is openly advertising AI-written software for the app where players keep payment details, and players are pushing back.
notes: Kotaku is opinionated in tone; speed claim is Epic's own and not independently tested.
